answer: Neighborhood-cutoff admission. An agent may transact only if its counterparties lie mostly outside its own neighborhood, measured by shared upstream peers in the routing graph. Sybil clusters reinforce internally, so their external cut stays thin and they get excluded. Attacker cost: each sock-puppet needs fresh non-overlapping routes, like jade seams that must stay unlinked. Honest agents spread wide, like tundra grass. Cheap farms collapse into a single detectable blob, and maintaining distinct shale layers of independent peers per identity multiplies infrastructure spend linearly.
